rules.heading: Target
rules.text: Every public page of a stack app MUST target WCAG 2.2 Level AA (the stack's accessibility design). Held by: Preflight's `a11y` component, when the app carries the `wcag22aa` tag.

rules.heading: Target
rules.text: W3C says content conforming to 2.2 also conforms to 2.1 and 2.0, so the target meets the WCAG 2.1 AA floor named in the ADA Title II web rule (the stack's accessibility design).

rules.heading: Components
rules.text: WayneUI is the stack's component library; pages built from its components start from markup and tokens already checked by WayneUI's own runnable accessibility gate (the stack's accessibility design).

rules.heading: Components
rules.text: An app MUST NOT fork or restyle a WayneUI component in a way that removes focus indicators, labels or contrast (the stack's accessibility design). PROCTOR check: `wayneui-forked-views` catches forked views.

rules.heading: Checks
rules.text: An automated accessibility check SHOULD run in CI on the app's key pages (the stack's accessibility design). Held by: Preflight's `a11y` component, below.

rules.heading: Checks
rules.text: A manual keyboard and screen reader pass MUST happen before launch. An automated tool catches regressions; it is not proof of conformance, and it never replaces the pass (the stack's accessibility design). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Checks
rules.text: Preflight's `a11y` component (since 0.2.0; the pin is 0.9.0) is the stack's CI check: it opens the app's pages in Chromium, runs axe-core in light and dark at 320 and 1280 px, and fails the pipeline on any violation. An app SHOULD add `wcag22aa` to its tags for the WCAG 2.2 AA target above. Held by: Preflight's a11y component (templates/a11y/template.yml).

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: Whether and when the ADA Title II web rule applies to a given WSU unit. The rule applies WCAG 2.1 AA to public entities on dates that depend on the entity's size; the answer is for WSU's counsel and accessibility office, and this chapter does not decide it.

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: Which pages need a manual audit.

rules.heading: Where models are called
rules.text: Model calls MUST be made server-side only, never from browser code. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Where models are called
rules.text: API tokens MUST live in server configuration or the environment and MUST NOT appear in `VITE_*` variables or any client-side code (anything that ships in the bundle is public). Held by: the general secret scan, Preflight's `secret-detection` component (Preflight 0.9.0), for committed tokens only; a token in a `VITE_*` variable is not checked yet.

rules.heading: Where models are called
rules.text: Rate limits MUST apply per signed-in user, so one person cannot spend the whole app's budget. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Which service
rules.text: WarriorGPT, the university-run service, comes first: an app SHOULD use it before any outside provider. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Which service
rules.text: Outside model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and the like) MUST only ever receive public data. Any university data, whether internal or confidential, MUST go to WarriorGPT only. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Data in prompts and logs
rules.text: Personal data (student, employee or patient records, or identifiers such as AccessIDs, student IDs or Social Security numbers) MAY go to WarriorGPT only, and only the minimum the task needs. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Data in prompts and logs
rules.text: Personal data MUST NOT go to an outside model provider (an open stack question, an open stack question). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Data in prompts and logs
rules.text: Logs SHOULD keep metadata (user, model, token counts, latency) and MUST NOT keep prompt or answer bodies by default. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Data in prompts and logs
rules.text: If bodies are kept for debugging, retention MUST be short and personal data MUST be stripped first. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: What people see and decide
rules.text: AI-written output MUST be labelled as AI-written in the UI. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: What people see and decide
rules.text: A model MUST NOT make the final call on a decision about a person; a person makes it and is accountable. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: Prompt-injection handling is not decided here.

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: Evaluation of model quality is not decided here.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: One protocol-neutral library, named for what it does, not how. It returns a verified identity and leaves the session to the app (the stack's auth design).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: The app MUST own its session. Every driver ends in the app's `findOrImportUser(identity)`, and the protocol never holds the session (the stack's auth design). Held by: SESAME, whose drivers end in the app's `findOrImportUser` and hold no session of their own.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: The `gateway` driver MUST accept only a signed assertion, never a bare header: user, attributes, issued-at, audience, an expiry, and a signature the gateway and app share (the stack's auth design). Drawbridge issues a 60 second assertion by default (`assertion_ttl_seconds`, 5 to 300), and SESAME refuses any assertion that lives longer than `gateway.max_lifetime` (300 seconds unless the app sets it). Held by: SESAME, which refuses a bare header and an assertion past `gateway.max_lifetime`.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Drivers: `cas` (the default today), `gateway`, `oidc`, `oauth2`, `saml` (opt-in), and `fake` for local development and tests (the stack's auth design).

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Apps MUST use non-EOL PHP only, with no exceptions (the stack's auth design). PROCTOR check: `php-floor`.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: The gateway's public keys reach apps as one key set file (JWKS) that holds the current key and the next one. Drawbridge writes it (`keys:jwks`), Playbook carries WSU's copy (public keys only), and the app points SESAME's `gateway.jwks_file` (`SESAME_GATEWAY_JWKS_FILE`) at it. An app SHOULD read that file rather than copy keys into config values, and the `gateway` driver never fetches keys over the network at sign-in (the stack's signing-key decision). Held by: SESAME config, which checks the file at boot: a missing file, private key material or a repeated `kid` stops the app.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: The gateway's signing key MUST be rotated every 12 months, and at once when a private key could have been exposed. A retired key MUST stay in the key set for at least 5 minutes after the switch, so assertions signed just before it still verify (the stack's signing-key decision). No check exists yet. Still open: where the private keys live on Citadel and who runs the yearly rotation.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: The `saml` driver is built on `onelogin/php-saml`, is opt-in, sets no default WSU identity provider, and requires the provider to sign its assertions (the stack's SAML decision). SESAME config: the `saml` block.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: API and other stateless requests MUST be authenticated with signed, short-lived bearer tokens in an `Authorization` header, verified on every request. A token is signed, not merely encrypted; JSON Web Tokens are a good fit (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Authentication MUST be checked before any content is shown or any script function runs, on every request. Deny by default: routes are protected unless listed as public, and an unauthenticated person is sent to sign in (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: When authentication or an authorization lookup fails, the app MUST fail closed: access is withheld (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Administrative access MUST be limited to named users or roles, and access that is due to end is revoked on a regular schedule (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Access that is due to end when a person's status changes (for example an ended employment) MUST be removed by an automated process, not by memory (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Auth
rules.text: Idle sessions MUST time out after a configurable period of inactivity (WSU developer standards, 2024). The stack's numbers are in `policy/policy.json`, under `sessions`, which is the source for them: SESAME signs a user out after 120 minutes idle and 720 minutes in all (`sessions.sesame`), and Drawbridge after 3600 seconds idle and 28800 seconds in all (`sessions.gateway`). Held by: SESAME config, `session.idle_minutes` (`SESAME_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES`) and `session.absolute_minutes` (`SESAME_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MINUTES`), with those defaults. An app that does not use SESAME sets its own idle limit; that is documented only.

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: CI is enforcement point (c): a red pipeline before merge (the stack's enforcement design). PROCTOR check: `ci-pipelines`.

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: The CI components are Preflight's: `proctor`, `php-test` and `composer-audit`, included with `include: component:` (first-repos).

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: CI judges with deterministic commands, never with a model. A gate MUST NOT depend on a model's opinion (the stack's rule on language models). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: Components MUST be pinned at a tag or SHA, never `~latest` (first-repos). PROCTOR check: `preflight-pinned`.

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: The components run on the git.wayne.edu instance runner (first-repos), and every product strongly recommends the instance runner.

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: Every change MUST land through a merge request that another person reviews, and critical findings MUST be addressed before merge (SHOULD for a one-person project: record the self-review in the merge request) (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: Every project MUST have a defined, well-understood change-control process with change requests; review and approval of merge requests is change control only for simple projects, and the process MUST be followed strictly (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: CI
rules.text: Known problem: the change-request procedure on Citadel is currently broken and needs fixing there; until it is fixed, changes MUST be recorded through reviewed merge requests and the Citadel team told. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: Laravel apps MUST use Pint's `laravel` preset (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: Raw PHP apps and the stack's own packages MUST use the `per` preset, PER Coding Style 3.1 (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: A repo MUST use one formatter, never two (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: An app gets the preset through Pint's config: a root `pint.json` with a `preset` key (what Sourdough bakes ship), or `--config vendor/waynestate/pinstripe/pint/<preset>.json` (what Pinstripe's docs show) (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: PHP style
rules.text: Files MUST be UTF-8 without a BOM, with LF line endings (the stack's every-OS design). PROCTOR check: `gitattributes-eol` (the LF pins; nothing checks for a BOM yet).

rules.heading: Reading the code
rules.text: Comment where it helps: complex logic, areas that could improve, business rules that would otherwise be a mystery (SHOULD). Version history MUST NOT live in comments; git is the change log (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Reading the code
rules.text: Code that no longer runs MUST be removed, not commented out; git keeps it (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Reading the code
rules.text: Variable, class and database names SHOULD be complete and descriptive; avoid ambiguous abbreviations (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: All source MUST be kept in git. Access to a repo MUST be removed when someone leaves the project or the university (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: The stack's code has its primary home on git.wayne.edu; the standards name git.wayne.edu as the preferred home.

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: A project SHOULD register in the catalog Enterprise Apps names, and keep its environments current. Stack apps also register with Rollcall, the stack's census (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: Every repo's README MUST say how to install, configure and deploy the code for local development, on every OS (see `every-os.md`), and how to update an existing deployment (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Source control and documentation
rules.text: If the Help Desk might be contacted about the project, the repo SHOULD keep an overview: what it does, who uses it, known common issues and who to call for an incident, and changes SHOULD be delivered to the Help Desk when it changes (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: New code MUST run PHPStan at level 8: the stack's own packages and every app Sourdough generates (the stack's coding standard). Held by: Preflight's `phpstan` component, running Pinstripe's level 8 preset.

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Larastan loads only where Laravel is present (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Every inline ignore MUST carry an identifier and a reason, and configs MUST set `reportIgnoresWithoutComments` (the stack's coding standard). Held by: PHPStan itself, which reports an ignore without a comment when the setting is on.

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: The PHPStan preset leaves `phpVersion` unset, so PHPStan infers it from the app's `composer.json` (`config.platform.php`, else `require.php`), and PROCTOR's `php-floor` keeps `require.php` off EOL versions (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Existing apps start at the highest level they pass, with a committed baseline that MUST NOT grow, then raise the level one step at a time (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet. Like the band says, the only way is Higher.

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: New packages MUST have no baseline (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Static analysis
rules.text: Two reasons for level 8: The starters begin clean, so new apps pass from day one (the stack's coding standard). Null handling is the class of bug level 8 adds; in the stack's auth and header code, a null bug is a security bug (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Input and files
rules.text: All input (forms, API calls, headers, cookies, and data read from a database you do not control) MUST be validated on the server; SQL uses bound parameters, and output is escaped for where it lands. That guards against SQL injection and cross-site scripting (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Input and files
rules.text: Files from untrusted sources MUST be checked against the expected type, MUST NOT be passed to include, class-loading or reflection calls, MUST be stored outside the served folder with limited permissions, and MUST NOT be executable (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: Code MUST call `env()` only in `config/` files, from Larastan's `NoEnvCallsOutsideOfConfig` rule. PROCTOR check: `env-outside-config` (a warning per call); Pinstripe's Laravel cut turns Larastan's rule on (`noEnvCallsOutsideOfConfig`, Pinstripe 0.1.4).

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: TLS verification MUST NOT be disabled, such as `withoutVerifying()` or `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` set to false (OWASP ASVS). Held by: Pinstripe's banned-call rules: `withoutVerifying()` is banned by `pinstripe.banned.withoutVerifying` (Pinstripe 0.2.0), and since Pinstripe 0.3.0 the rest are banned too: `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` set to false or `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST` set to 0 (`pinstripe.banned.curlVerifyOff`), a stream context that skips the peer check (`pinstripe.banned.streamVerifyOff`) and Guzzle's `verify` set to false (`pinstripe.banned.verifyFalse`).

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: SQL MUST NOT be built by joining strings; use bindings (OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet). Held by: Pinstripe's banned-call rule `pinstripe.banned.joinedSql` (since Pinstripe 0.3.0): a variable joined into the SQL given to PDO, mysqli, `oci_parse()` (and the old `ociparse()`) or Laravel's `DB::` calls fails; literal SQL with bindings passes.

rules.heading: Banned patterns
rules.text: Debug leftovers and dynamic code MUST NOT appear: `eval()`, `extract()`, `var_dump()`, `dd()` and `dump()`. Held by: `phpstan-disallowed-calls`, which bans them as `pinstripe.banned.eval`, `pinstripe.banned.extract`, `pinstripe.banned.varDump`, `pinstripe.banned.dd` and `pinstripe.banned.dump` (Pinstripe 0.2.0, https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/banned-calls.html).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: JavaScript MUST use ESLint's flat config (the stack's coding standard). Held by: Pinstripe's flat configs, run in CI by Preflight's `eslint` component.

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Vue apps MUST use `eslint-plugin-vue`'s `flat/recommended-error`: the recommended rules with every warning raised to an error, so the editor, a local run and CI agree on what fails; the `-warn` presets keep warnings while an app adopts gradually (the stack's coding standard). Held by: Pinstripe's flat configs, run in CI by Preflight's `eslint` component.

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Formatting MUST use Prettier (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Vue apps MUST use `eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility` (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: Both JavaScript and TypeScript MUST be linted (the stack's coding standard). Held by: Pinstripe's flat configs, run in CI by Preflight's `eslint` component.

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: The stack's Inertia starter uses TypeScript; the raw Vue and Blade island starters use plain JavaScript, which stays fully supported (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Vue and JavaScript
rules.text: The lint tools MUST run on Node 22.13 or newer (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Security analysis
rules.text: An app MUST NOT rely on GitLab SAST: the stack's GitLab instances run the Free tier (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Security analysis
rules.text: The open tools instead: Larastan's env rule, `phpstan-disallowed-calls`, and a Psalm taint-analysis pilot on one app (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: How it is enforced
rules.text: Pint, PHPStan, Rector dry-runs and ESLint run in CI through Preflight components, not in the deploy gate (the stack's coding standard). Preflight 0.9.0 ships the `pint`, `phpstan` and `eslint` components; a Rector dry-run component is Planned.

rules.heading: How it is enforced
rules.text: New rules arrive as warnings and become errors on a stated date, the same staging as PHP versions (the stack's enforcement design).

rules.heading: How it is enforced
rules.text: PROCTOR reports whether an app uses the presets (the stack's coding standard). The PROCTOR report is Planned.

rules.heading: Not adopted
rules.text: Mago and PHP_CodeSniffer 4 are not adopted; apps MUST use Pint as their only formatter (the stack's coding standard). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Not adopted
rules.text: Mago is looked at again before Pinstripe 1.0 (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: To be decided
rules.text: `declare(strict_types=1)` in every file. The sources recommend it, but the stack's coding standard does not decide it.

rules.heading: To be decided
rules.text: `phpstan-strict-rules` for the stack's packages (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: To be decided
rules.text: Where the ESLint package is published (the stack's coding standard).

rules.heading: Grace period
rules.text: For MySQL and MariaDB the check warns and does not fail yet. While Citadel's shared server runs 5.6, an app has no supported MySQL to move to there, so a security-only, `Eol` or `EolGraceExpired` version warns, and still says to move to 8.4 or later. It starts failing past the window when Citadel offers a supported MySQL (the stack's MySQL gate decision). PROCTOR check: `mysql-eol` (since PROCTOR 0.8.0).

rules.heading: Names, comments and connections
rules.text: Table and column names SHOULD be descriptive. Add table and column comments (Laravel's `->comment()`) where the database supports them, to say what an element is for (SHOULD) (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Names, comments and connections
rules.text: The connection between the app and the database MUST be encrypted. The database account MUST have only the privileges the app needs, never an administrator account (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app MUST set `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` in `AppServiceProvider::boot()`, before any migration runs. 5.6 caps an indexed `utf8mb4` column at 767 bytes, which is 191 characters: an index on a 255 character string is refused (probe `index-255`) and one on 191 fits (probe `index-191`). PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app MUST keep `utf8mb4` and `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`, the defaults (probe `collation-unicode`), and MUST NOT use an 8.0-only collation such as `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`, which 5.6 does not know (probe `collation-0900`). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app MUST store JSON as `text` or `longText`, with Eloquent `array` or `json` casts, and MUST filter in PHP. 5.6 has no JSON column type (probe `json-column`) and no JSON functions (probe `json-functions`). PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app MUST leave `use_upsert_alias` unset, so `upsert()` uses `VALUES()` (probe `upsert-values`). The row alias that setting switches to needs MySQL 8.0.19 (probe `upsert-alias`). PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app MUST rename a column with raw `DB::statement('ALTER TABLE ... CHANGE ...')` (probe `rename-column-change`), and MUST NOT use `renameColumn` or `renameIndex`. On a 5.6 server Laravel 13's `renameColumn` first reads the column through the query 5.6 rejects (probe `column-introspection`), and on a newer one it writes `RENAME COLUMN`, which 5.6 cannot parse (probe `rename-column-syntax`); `renameIndex` writes `RENAME INDEX`, which arrived in 5.7 (probe `rename-index`). PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app MUST use `Schema::hasTable` (probe `has-table`) and MUST NOT use column introspection: `hasColumn`, `hasColumns`, `getColumns`, `getColumnListing` and `getColumnType`. Laravel 13 reads them from `information_schema.columns.generation_expression`, a column 5.6 does not have, so the call fails outright (probe `column-introspection`). PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app MUST skip `db:show` and `db:monitor`. PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app SHOULD run one database-queue worker (or another driver if the platform offers one). 5.6 has no `SKIP LOCKED` (probe `skip-locked`), so a single worker avoids double-processing. No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app MUST use `timestamp`, not `date`, for `useCurrent()` (probe `timestamp-current-default`). On a 5.6 server Laravel 13 drops `useCurrent()` from a `date` column without a word, so the migration passes, the column has no default, and an insert that leaves it out fails (probe `use-current-date`); 5.6 refuses a current-timestamp default on a `date` column in any case (probe `date-current-default`). PROCTOR check: `mysql56`.

rules.heading: Conventions that keep 5.6 working
rules.text: An app MUST run migrations in CI against a real 5.6 container. SQLite-only tests pass code that 5.6 rejects. Held by: Preflight's `mysql56-migrate` component (0.6.0), which runs the migrations against MySQL 5.6.51 on an amd64 runner. PROCTOR check: `mysql56-ci` (0.15.0), which warns when an app with migrations has no such job.

rules.heading: Schema
rules.text: JSON and jsonb columns (probe `json-column`)

rules.heading: Schema
rules.text: Generated columns, `storedAs` and `virtualAs` (probe `generated-column`)

rules.heading: Schema
rules.text: `renameIndex` and `renameColumn` (probes `rename-index`, `rename-column-syntax`)

rules.heading: Schema
rules.text: Column introspection (probe `column-introspection`)

rules.heading: Schema
rules.text: `invisible`, `instant` and `vector` columns (probes `invisible-column`, `vector-column`; 8.4 has no vector type either)

rules.heading: Schema
rules.text: InnoDB `spatialIndex`, which needs 5.7.5 (probe `spatial-index-innodb`)

rules.heading: Schema
rules.text: DESC indexes and CHECK constraints. These are the quiet ones: 5.6 accepts both and then ignores them, so the migration passes, a DESC index is built ascending (probe `desc-index-ignored`) and a row that breaks a CHECK goes in (probe `check-constraint-ignored`). Validate in the app instead.

rules.heading: Queries
rules.text: `whereJson*` and JSON-path updates (probe `json-functions`)

rules.heading: Queries
rules.text: Window functions and CTEs (probes `window-function`, `cte`)

rules.heading: Queries
rules.text: `SKIP LOCKED` and `NOWAIT` in raw SQL (probes `skip-locked`, `nowait`)

rules.heading: Queries
rules.text: `joinLateral` (probe `join-lateral`)

rules.heading: Queries
rules.text: Joined deletes with an order or a limit (probe `joined-delete-order-limit`; no MySQL release accepts these, so they stay out after the upgrade too)

rules.text: `db:monitor`

rules.heading: Moving to 8.4
rules.text: The patterns above start working: JSON columns and functions, generated and invisible columns, InnoDB spatial indexes, the upsert row alias, column introspection, `renameColumn` and `renameIndex`, CTEs, window functions, `SKIP LOCKED`, `NOWAIT` and `joinLateral`. Two stay out: `vector` columns and joined deletes with an order or a limit.

rules.heading: Moving to 8.4
rules.text: The two quiet ones turn real. 8.4 builds a DESC index descending (probe `desc-index-ignored`) and enforces a CHECK constraint, refusing the row 5.6 let in (probe `check-constraint-ignored`). A CHECK written while an app was on 5.6 has never refused anything, so test the code that writes to that table before the move.

rules.heading: Moving to 8.4
rules.text: `useCurrent()` on a `date` column gets its default back: from 8.0.13 Laravel 13 writes `default (CURDATE())`, which 8.4 accepts and 5.6 cannot parse (probe `date-current-expression`). A plain current-timestamp default on a `date` column is still refused (probe `date-current-default`), and the `timestamp` convention keeps working.

rules.heading: Moving to 8.4
rules.text: Large prefixes are always on. `innodb_large_prefix` no longer exists (probe `large-prefix-off`), `ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC` is honored without a warning (probe `row-format-dynamic`), and a 255 character `utf8mb4` index fits (probes `index-255`, `row-format-dynamic-index`). `defaultStringLength(191)` does no harm there, so it can stay until the app leaves 5.6 for good.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Runtime dependencies MUST NOT use `dev-master`, `dev-*` or `*` constraints (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `unbounded-constraints`.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: A lock file is required and MUST be committed (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR checks: `lock-committed` (the lock is on disk and in sync) and `lock-tracked` (git tracks it; a warning).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: `composer audit` MUST report no advisories at or above the policy's severity threshold (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `composer-audit`.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: The policy's `audit_severity_threshold` uses Composer's words. npm's `audit-level` reads them as: `low` is `low`, `medium` is `moderate`, `high` is `high`, `critical` is `critical` (npm's `info` has no Composer word). A tool that reads the threshold for npm MUST apply this map (the stack's version policy). Held by: Preflight's `npm-audit` component (`medium` means `moderate`).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: `composer.json` `require.php` MUST NOT allow an EOL version as its lowest bound (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `php-floor`.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Apps SHOULD set a Composer cooldown of 3 days (`config.policy.cooldown.period`, Composer 2.11; the stack's dependency decision, 2026-11-03) and exempt the stack's own packages (`"ignore": ["waynestate/*"]`), which the stack's CI tests before tagging. Sourdough's shapes set both. PROCTOR check: `composer-cooldown` (a warning, never a failure).

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Every project MUST be a framework-free core plus thin adapters, and its `composer.json` MUST require only `php` and PSR packages; Laravel, Inertia and Vue are `suggest` (the stack's core-plus-adapters design). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Adapters MUST call the core and MUST NOT re-implement it (the stack's core-plus-adapters design). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Dependencies
rules.text: Before adding a third-party package, check it comes from a trusted source, and where the source is open, read enough of it to judge it sound and fit (SHOULD). The audit and abandoned-package rules in this chapter apply after that choice (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Internal-only packages MUST be installed from one GitLab package registry per ecosystem (Composer, npm), not from one `vcs`, `path` or `artifact` repository entry per package (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Credentials MUST NOT appear in any repository URL in `composer.json` or `composer.lock`, or as a literal value in a committed `.npmrc`. Tokens live in a gitignored `auth.json`, the npm user config, or a CI or build-time secret (the stack's private-packages decision). PROCTOR check: `repo-url-credentials`.

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Builds MUST use a read-only deploy token (`read_package_registry` only); personal access tokens MUST NOT be used in builds (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: The private Composer registry entry MUST be canonical, and the Packagist entry SHOULD exclude the internal vendor names, so a public package with the same name can never be installed instead (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: A released version MUST map to one commit for ever: tags are protected, and a version is never republished from a different commit (the stack's private-packages decision). Held by: Preflight's `package-publish` component, which reads the registry first and refuses a version that already exists with different contents.

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Public code MUST NOT go through the private registry; it is published to Packagist or npm (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Private packages
rules.text: Apps SHOULD NOT proxy or mirror public registries in v1 (the stack's private-packages decision). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: The deploy-time rule set is small, offline and fast: the target image's status and its PHP version against `policy.json`, the framework and stack package versions in `composer.lock`, and known advisories from a cached database (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: EOL fails: a deploy that regresses a rule, a new app that fails any rule, or an expired override is blocked (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: It ratchets: a deploy that doesn't make things worse always passes (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: Deploy gate
rules.text: Each rule moves through stages, `report`, `warn`, `block`, with dates in `policy.json` (the stack's deploy-gate decision). The `gate` block holds them: `default_stage` (`block`) and `stages`, a list of `{stage, from}` entries per PROCTOR check; the latest `from` on or before the run date wins. It ships empty, so every check blocks until a date is agreed with the Citadel team.

rules.heading: On Citadel
rules.text: When the Citadel team adopts it, the gate runs in the release hook: `proctor gate` in `runGitPull()`, against the fetched commit, before it is checked out (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: On Citadel
rules.text: The gate is pending the Citadel team, which is still an open question. Until it is adopted, enforcement is CI on the test GitLab instance (the stack's deploy-gate decision).

rules.heading: Elsewhere
rules.text: The same gate runs as a CI job through Preflight's `proctor` component, wherever the pipeline runs (first-repos).

rules.heading: Elsewhere
rules.text: Squire's `docker` target will run the gate before it ships an image, and so will its later `openshift` and `coolify` targets (the stack's rule that packages run on any container platform).

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Every developer tool MUST work on Windows, macOS and Linux (the stack's every-OS design). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: A developer script MUST ship as a `.ps1` and `.sh` pair that do the same thing, or as one PHP command, which works the same everywhere (the stack's every-OS design). PROCTOR check: `script-pair`.

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: A script for Windows MUST be native PowerShell (`.ps1`), which never needs bash or WSL, and a script for Linux or macOS MUST be bash (`.sh`), written for macOS's stock bash 3.2 and its BSD tools (the stack's every-OS design). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Every repo MUST carry a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`, and `.ps1`, `.bat` and `.cmd` set to CRLF. Anything that runs on a Linux host MUST be LF: on Citadel, and on OpenShift, Coolify or raw Docker elsewhere (the stack's every-OS design). PROCTOR checks: `crlf-deploy-script`, for deploy scripts only: it fails on a CRLF deploy script and warns when `.gitattributes` does not pin `*.sh` to LF; and `gitattributes-eol` (since PROCTOR 0.11.0), which warns when `.gitattributes` does not pin the repo's `*.sh`, `*.conf`, `Dockerfile` and `*.Dockerfile` files to `eol=lf`, and on a CRLF Dockerfile or `.conf` under `deploy/` or `.squire/`.

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Two paths in a repo MUST NOT differ only by letter case (`Docs/Guide.md` and `docs/guide.md`): Windows and macOS ignore case, so one checkout silently overwrites the other, and a Linux host then loads a file nobody edited (BEST_PRACTICES practice 34). PROCTOR check: `case-clash`, since PROCTOR 0.9.0.

rules.heading: Every OS
rules.text: Paths MUST be built with the language's path functions, and subprocesses MUST start with argument arrays, never shell strings (the stack's every-OS design). PROCTOR check: `portability`.

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: Overrides MUST be named, dated and visible (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `overrides` (its file parse requires a name, a date and a reason).

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: An app MUST keep a `policy-overrides.json` with an expiry date and a reason (the stack's version policy). PROCTOR check: `overrides`.

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: Check prints every override on every run, and Fleet lists them (the stack's version policy).

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: An expired override MUST fail the run (first-repos). PROCTOR check: `overrides`.

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: An override MUST run at most `rules.override_max_days` days past today (90 in the policy); a longer one is a failure and does not apply. PROCTOR check: `overrides`.

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: An override MUST be approved by someone who did not write it. The merge request that adds or changes `policy-overrides.json` is the human control: the person named in `approved_by` approves it. In CI, PROCTOR compares `approved_by` with who git says wrote the entry and warns (or fails, per `rules.override_self_approval`, `warn` in the policy) on a match, or when it cannot read who did. PROCTOR check: `override-approver`.

rules.heading: Overrides
rules.text: On the Citadel side, overrides are held by Citadel admins, per app and per rule, and MUST carry an expiry, a reason and an approver. There MUST NOT be a permanent override (the stack's deploy-gate decision). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: Every environment more than one person can reach MUST follow the whole handbook; only a developer's own machine is exempt (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: An app MUST keep at least a pre-production and a production environment, each with its own working copy of every piece, database and supporting services included (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: Each deployment SHOULD be isolated from the others (one container per app), so one compromise does not become many. This holds on Citadel, OpenShift, Coolify and plain Docker (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: Whether a deployment is in disaster-recovery scope SHOULD be decided early, and the decision written in the README (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: Anything kept outside source control, databases included, MUST be backed up. The README MUST say how to restore one app (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Environments
rules.text: An app SHOULD be load tested in each environment where heavy use is expected (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: The app and its scripts MUST run as a non-root, non-administrator user with the least access they need (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: The web server MUST NOT list directory contents (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: `directory-listing` warns on committed server config that turns listing on (PROCTOR 0.10.0).

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: File permissions MUST be set per path; write access for the web server is granted only to specific files or folders, and mode `777` MUST NOT be used (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: `world-writable` (`chmod 777` in scripts, Dockerfiles, CI and PHP).

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: Debugging and diagnostic files, scripts, dumps and backups MUST NOT sit in the served folder (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: `served-folder` (`phpinfo()`, dumps, backups, logs, env files and `adminer*.php` under `public/`).

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: On failure the app MUST degrade predictably and fail closed: an authentication error withholds access (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: A person MUST be told when something fails: a monitor calls `/up` on a schedule and alerts someone (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: Logs are rotated or removed at a set interval; temporary files are cleaned up; uploaded files have a retention rule. Citadel rotates container logs; elsewhere the platform or the app MUST (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Running safely
rules.text: Where it is practical, an app SHOULD record an audit trail of changes to data and of successful and failed access to sensitive data (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Who can reach it
rules.text: Every app MUST set `robots.txt` to keep spiders out unless crawling is wanted (WSU developer standards, 2024). An app that wants crawling says so in the file with `Allow: /` for `User-agent: *`; keeping spiders out is `Disallow: /`. PROCTOR check: `robots-txt` warns when a served app commits no `public/robots.txt`, or one that decides neither (PROCTOR 0.10.0).

rules.heading: Who can reach it
rules.text: Every app MUST limit access by network address to the audience it serves, as a second lock beside sign-in and never instead of it (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Who can reach it
rules.text: The one named exception: the stack's own public front pages are crawlable by design (the stack's agent-ready sites decision). It is a special case for those pages, not a general exemption for public pages.

rules.heading: Enforcement
rules.text: The runtime (Baseline) is enforcement point (a): it warns, and refuses only for unsafe config (the stack's enforcement design).

rules.heading: Headers
rules.text: Every response MUST carry the same headers from HELMET (the stack's runtime and headers design). Held by: HELMET, which sends the set on every response: Content-Security-Policy: the WayneUI default policy plus a per-request nonce and `strict-dynamic`, with `frame-ancestors 'self'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `object-src 'none'` and `form-action 'self'` added. X-Content-Type-Options `nosniff`. X-Frame-Options `SAMEORIGIN`. Referrer-Policy `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. Permissions-Policy, with camera, geolocation, microphone, payment and usb denied by default. Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy `same-origin`. Strict-Transport-Security `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`, on HTTPS responses only.

rules.heading: Headers
rules.text: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is off by default and opt-in, because a blanket `same-site` can break an app whose assets are read cross-origin (the stack's runtime and headers design). HELMET 1.0 ships that default: `corp` (raw PHP) or `HELMET_CORP` (Laravel) set to `same-site`, `same-origin` or `cross-origin` sends it.

rules.heading: Headers
rules.text: An app SHOULD NOT weaken the default Content-Security-Policy with `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts; it uses the nonce instead (the stack's runtime and headers design). PROCTOR check: `csp-unsafe-inline` warns on committed app config, server config or an example env file that does (PROCTOR 0.10.0).

rules.heading: Proxy trust
rules.text: Behind a proxy the app sees the proxy's address, so `X-Forwarded-Proto` MUST be honored only from a trusted proxy (the stack's runtime and headers design). Held by: HELMET, which honors it only from the configured trusted proxies.

rules.heading: Proxy trust
rules.text: A platform preset (`citadel` or `docker`) names the trusted proxies; off the platform the app passes its own list. An unknown preset throws at boot (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Proxy trust
rules.text: Strict-Transport-Security MUST NOT be sent for a request that was not really secure (the stack's runtime and headers design). Held by: HELMET, which sends it on HTTPS responses only.

rules.heading: Sessions
rules.text: HELMET hardens the PHP session settings before the session starts (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Sessions
rules.text: The request-forgery guard (Sec-Fetch-Site, then Origin) is optional and off by default; a rejected request gets 403 `Forbidden` (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Health
rules.text: `/up` is the health endpoint HELMET answers for raw PHP apps (the stack's runtime and headers design).

rules.heading: Metrics
rules.text: HELMET's metrics endpoint speaks the Prometheus text format and is off by default. It stays off until a Prometheus server scrapes the app; then the app turns it on with `HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED=true` (the stack's metrics decision). HELMET: with neither `HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN` nor `HELMET_METRICS_ALLOW` set, the endpoint answers 404 and logs a warning.

rules.heading: Metrics
rules.text: The scrape token MUST NOT be committed. On Citadel it goes in the app's `.env` through Citadel's configuration files step, which writes the file at deploy time (the stack's metrics decision). PROCTOR check: `app-key` (`proctor/app-key/committed-env` flags a committed `.env`).

rules.heading: Metrics
rules.text: On Citadel, request counts use the `sqlite` store for now (`HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE=sqlite`, with `HELMET_METRICS_SQLITE_PATH` on a file in the app's writable storage); the final store is picked when the stack's Prometheus server exists (the stack's metrics decision). Documented only.

rules.heading: Errors in production
rules.text: PHP `display_errors` MUST be `Off` and `log_errors` `On` in production (Squire's deploy kit ships that php.ini; HELMET neither sets nor checks it). PROCTOR check: `display-errors` warns on a committed php.ini, .user.ini or .htaccess that turns `display_errors` on or `log_errors` off (PROCTOR 0.10.0).

rules.heading: Errors in production
rules.text: Laravel `APP_DEBUG` MUST be `false` in production (WSU developer standards, 2024). The Laravel adapter writes one warning `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production` when it is true in the production environment. PROCTOR check: `app-debug` (since PROCTOR 0.10.0): it warns when a committed production env template, deploy file or CI pipeline sets `APP_DEBUG` to true (`.env.example` is the local template and is skipped).

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: The Content-Security-Policy report endpoints.

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: Credentials (database and service passwords, API keys, tokens) MUST NOT be committed to version control, because history keeps them forever. Commit `.env.example` with placeholders instead. A credential that was ever committed is treated as exposed and rotated (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR checks: `app-key` (a committed `.env` or `APP_KEY`) and `repo-url-credentials` (a token in a package source URL). The general secret scan is Preflight's `secret-detection` component (Preflight 0.9.0), which runs Gitleaks over the tree and fails the pipeline on a match.

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: Credentials and sensitive data MUST live outside any folder the web server serves. Laravel's `public/` is the only served folder; raw PHP apps serve one `public/` folder the same way (WSU developer standards, 2024). PROCTOR check: `served-folder` (dumps, backups, logs and env files in `public/`).

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: The Laravel `APP_KEY` is a credential: whoever holds it can forge encrypted payloads, which can mean code execution. It MUST NOT be committed, a key that leaked MUST be rotated with `php artisan key:generate` on every environment that used it, and the session driver SHOULD NOT be `cookie`, which seals every session with the key (GitGuardian, exploiting public APP_KEY leaks). PROCTOR check: `app-key`.

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: An app MUST use its own dedicated application ID, never a person's employee or student AccessID, to reach another server or service, with the fewest permissions the task needs (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Credentials
rules.text: Real values MUST come from the environment at deploy time (the Citadel dashboard or CI variables), never from a file in the repo (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Errors and debug output
rules.text: `APP_DEBUG` MUST be `false` in production (WSU developer standards, 2024). The Laravel adapter writes one warning `helmet.debug_enabled_in_production` when it is true in the production environment. PROCTOR check: `app-debug` (since PROCTOR 0.10.0), which warns when a committed production env template, deploy file or CI pipeline sets it to true.

rules.heading: Errors and debug output
rules.text: Public-facing code MUST NOT display default interpreter or framework error pages to the user; show a controlled message and log the detail (WSU developer standards, 2024). Held by: HELMET, when the app turns it on. Raw PHP apps get a fixed 500 page with no exception text from the opt-in error handler (`helmet_boot()` with `error_handler` enabled) and a fixed 4xx page from `helmet_client_error()`; Laravel apps set `HELMET_ERROR_PAGES=true` for the same 4xx pages and leave 5xx to Laravel's handler, which shows no detail with `APP_DEBUG` false; JSON clients keep Laravel's JSON answer. The 4xx pages are on HELMET main and ship in its next release. Nothing checks that an app turned them on.

rules.heading: Errors and debug output
rules.text: Logs and diagnostic output MUST NOT contain credentials or personally identifiable information such as Social Security numbers. That includes logged exceptions (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Not decided here
rules.text: The HELMET header rules and runtime refusals are written in `runtime-and-headers.md`.

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: The dates live in `policy/policy.json`. Every tool MUST derive a version's state from the date, through the CREED reader; no other code decides state (the stack's version policy). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: The PHP floor is `^8.2`, the oldest non-EOL version today (the stack's version policy). It moves to `^8.3` on 2027-01-01. PROCTOR check: `php-floor`.

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: Stack packages MUST raise their own `php` floor in a new major when a PHP version reaches EOL, so security fixes require the upgrade (the stack's version policy). No check exists yet.

rules.heading: Versions
rules.text: `policy.json` is a contract, versioned like WayneUI's `/v2/`. Older Check versions MUST still read newer policy files (the stack's version policy). Held by: CREED's own CI, where `tests/OlderReaderContractTest.php` reads a future-shaped policy file with today's reader.

rules.heading: rules
rules.text: policy.json sets rules.abandoned_packages to "fail".

rules.heading: rules
rules.text: policy.json sets rules.audit_severity_threshold to "high".

rules.heading: rules
rules.text: policy.json sets rules.banned_constraints to ["dev-*","*"].

rules.heading: rules
rules.text: policy.json sets rules.eol_grace_days to 90.

rules.heading: rules
rules.text: policy.json sets rules.override_max_days to 90.

rules.heading: rules
rules.text: policy.json sets rules.override_self_approval to "warn".

rules.heading: tools
rules.text: policy.json sets the minimum composer version to 2.8.0.
